note: This needs, per segment (SME, LAM, KAM), the customer with the least 2013 CZK annual consumption (an argmin on THE SUM), then that same customer's annual AVERAGE consumption (a different aggregate), then pairwise arithmetic differences of those three per-segment scalars. I could get each per-segment value individually and correctly with one query each -- e.g. for SME: 'LIST c, t_sum, t_avg FROM Yearmonth ym has Customer c [has CustomerSegment: 'SME'] [has CustomerCurrency: 'CZK'] AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d1 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v1 AND ALSO THE SUM OF v1 GROUPED BY c AS t_sum AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d2 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v2 AND ALSO THE AVERAGE v2 GROUPED BY c AS t_avg WHERE starts_with(d1, '2013') AND starts_with(d2, '2013') ORDERED WITH t_sum ASCENDING THE FIRST 1' (gives customer 12685, average -7003.55; the same pattern gives customer 50066/average 1.12 for LAM and customer 45195/average -755.55 for KAM). But there is no construct in the primer, and none I could get to parse, for combining three independently-filtered 'argmin row' selections into one query and taking arithmetic differences between them: a (LIST ...) used as a scalar operand does not respect its own ORDERED/FIRST (silently gave a wrong, differently-ordered value), an aggregate cannot be taken over an already-GROUPED BY result ('t' IN names an attribute the path does not bind'), and FROM cannot take a parenthesised sub-SELECT as its source. So the per-segment lookups are individually expressible but the three-way combination into pairwise differences is not, as a single ConQuer-92 query against this model.
